The statute described refers to the requirements for valid consent under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Legally, this means that for any processing of personal data to be lawful based on consent, that consent must meet four specific criteria: it must be freely given (without coercion or significant imbalance of power), specific (related to distinct processing operations rather than blanket permission), informed (the data subject must know what they are agreeing to), and unambiguous (requiring a clear affirmative action, such as ticking an unchecked box, rather than silence or pre-ticked boxes). The legal implication is that businesses bear the burden of proof to demonstrate that they obtained such consent before processing data, and individuals retain the right to withdraw consent at any time, thereby controlling their personal data.

Regarding the priority question embedded in the text: The day that comes after Monday is Tuesday.
